decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Aerodactyl + Arcanine lead provides immediate double blunting: Wide Guard counters Heat Wave and Earthquake while Intimidate and Snarl neutralize physical and special attackers. Dragonite and Mega Gengar form a powerful cleanup backline with ExtremeSpeed priority and Shadow Tag trapping against low-HP foes.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash; Sleep Powder, Earth Power, Sludge Bomb), Jolly Scarf Garchomp (Dragon Claw, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Poison Jab), Modest Life Orb Primarina (Liquid Voice, Protect). Goodra-H and Talonflame left on bench. Plan: Maintain Aerodactyl + Arcanine priority/speed control core; use Wide Guard/Snarl to blunt spread moves and enable Mega Gengar + Dragonite cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega is Charizard-Y, saved for after Aerodactyl is removed. Talonflame and Primarina’s turn-one job is to eliminate Aerodactyl through its Focus Sash with two targeted attacks; Wide Guard cannot stop that. Charizard-Y then supplies sun-powered Heat Wave/Solar Beam pressure, while Scarf Garchomp covers Arcanine, Krookodile, and Dragonite.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt; targeted double pressure removes it through Sash and avoids Wide Guard. Mega Gengar is Timid with Protect and Shadow Tag. Dragonite is Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl; preserve a healthy answer to priority cleanup. Against the Aero/Arcanine structure, avoid leading Charizard-Y into Aerodactyl when a targeted Aero-removal lead is available.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame gets priority +1 Tailwind via Gale Wings. By using Tailwind with Aerodactyl, we match speed control; under double Tailwind, Arcanine (230) remains faster than Modest Primarina (max 224). This guarantees Arcanine gets off a spread Snarl before Primarina moves, dropping her SpA and blunting her burst damage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash), Jolly Scarf Garchomp, Modest LO Primarina (Liquid Voice), Goodra-H, Talonflame (Charti Berry). Plan: Maintain speed control with Aerodactyl Tailwind to ensure Arcanine Snarls before special attackers hit.

decisions.rationale: Gengar takes advantage of 4 turns of Tailwind to outspeed both opposing Pokémon. Mega Evolving Gengar next turn locks Primarina and Talonflame on the field with Shadow Tag while both have -1 SpA and -1 Atk from Arcanine's Intimidate and Snarl, allowing Gengar to eliminate Primarina with Sludge Bomb before taking damage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash), Jolly Scarf Garchomp, Modest LO Primarina (Liquid Voice, Psychic Noise), Goodra-H, Talonflame (Charti Berry). Plan: Maintain speed control with Tailwind and use Gengar Shadow Tag to trap debuffed foes.

decisions.rationale: Targeted double pressure is the cleanest Aerodactyl removal through Focus Sash and cannot be stopped by Wide Guard. It denies its Tailwind if both attacks connect, while Charti Berry gives Talonflame its best chance to absorb Rock Slide. Tailwind alone leaves Aerodactyl alive at Sash and able to act.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt; targeted double pressure removes it through Sash and avoids Wide Guard. Mega Gengar is Timid with Protect and Shadow Tag. Dragonite is Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl; preserve a healthy answer to priority cleanup. Against Aero/Arcanine, avoid leading Charizard-Y into Aerodactyl when targeted Aero removal is available.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, Gengar and Arcanine both outspeed the opposing active Pokemon. Combining Extreme Speed from Arcanine with Mega Gengar's 2x super-effective Sludge Bomb guarantees a KO on Primarina before it can execute an attack, while Shadow Tag traps Talonflame at -1 Attack.

Set Tailwind now so the back line can exploit the speed swing once opposing Tailwind ends. Psychic Noise is the only listed super-effective pressure on Gengar and discourages a free attack; if it Protects, we gain our Tailwind safely and retain Primarina.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is Timid with Protect and Shadow Tag. Dragonite is Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl; preserve a healthy answer to priority cleanup. Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt. Against Aero/Arcanine, avoid leading Charizard-Y into Aerodactyl when targeted Aero removal is available.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is the stronger replacement: Talonflame is immune to its Earthquake, letting it threaten both Mega Gengar and Arcanine immediately. Choice Scarf plus our Tailwind also gives the best chance to act before Mega Gengar despite its opposing Tailwind.

Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Mega Gengar under Tailwind and heavily threatens both active slots with Earthquake. Gengar must Protect to stay healthy and maintain Shadow Tag lock. Arcanine switches out to Dragonite, which is immune to Ground, preserving Arcanine's Intimidate/HP for later while safely positioning Dragonite's 4x super-effective Ice Spinner against Garchomp next turn.

Garchomp moves first under Scarf plus Tailwind and Earthquake is super-effective into both foes while Talonflame is immune as a Flying type. Protect denies the likely priority or Gengar-targeted attempt to remove Talonflame; if Gengar Protects, Earthquake still removes or heavily damages Arcanine. Taunt is unreliable because Mega Gengar can outspeed Talonflame under opposing Tailwind.

Garchomp is Scarf-locked into Earthquake and outspeeds Gengar under Tailwind. Gengar must switch out to avoid a free KO. Switching Gengar to Arcanine fires Intimidate, pivoting Arcanine into the spread EQ while Dragonite is immune to Ground and safely OHKOs Garchomp with 4x Ice Spinner.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash), Jolly Scarf Garchomp (locked EQ), Modest LO Primarina (fainted), Goodra-H, Talonflame (-1 Atk Charti Berry).

decisions.rationale: Earthquake guarantees Mega Gengar’s KO if its reduced-success Protect fails, while Talonflame renews Tailwind and stays immune to Earthquake. Maintaining speed is more valuable than weak, Intimidate-reduced Brave Bird damage into Dragonite; Dragonite cannot stop the immediate Gengar pressure before Garchomp moves.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Charizard cannot KO Dragonite under any circumstances (resists Fire, Grass, immune to Ground). Extreme Speed (+2 priority) from Arcanine chips Charizard before Tailwind-boosted Charizard can attack, guaranteeing Dragonite's 4x super-effective Rock Slide secures the KO even against maximum physical bulk. Rock Slide also heavily damages Talonflame through Charti Berry while Tailwind expires at turn end.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash), Jolly Scarf Garchomp, Modest LO Primarina, Goodra-H, Talonflame (-1 Atk Charti Berry).

decisions.rationale: Taunt denies Dragonite Protect before it acts and forces its likely Rock Slide into Charizard’s Protect. Mega Evolution activates Drought while retaining guaranteed raw Speed over both remaining foes after Tailwind ends. This preserves Charizard to remove Arcanine with Scorching Sands next turn; attacking Arcanine now exposes Charizard to Dragonite’s guaranteed Rock Slide OHKO.

Charizard-Mega-Y is the opponent's last Pokémon. Arcanine's +2 priority Extreme Speed chips Charizard first, ensuring Dragonite's 4x super-effective Life Orb Rock Slide comfortably achieves a 100% KO range even if Charizard outspeeds at +0 priority. Charizard cannot KO Dragonite from 68% HP with any move.

Heat Wave is the only line that pressures both remaining foes and can capitalize on Rock Slide’s accuracy risk. Scorching Sands leaves Dragonite untouched, while reduced-success Protect only delays the unavoidable Rock Slide pressure. Dragonite is Taunted, so it cannot shield itself from Heat Wave.

Double Extreme Speed provides +2 priority, 100% accurate chip into Charizard-Mega-Y before it can move. Even if Charizard survives the double priority hit and attacks with Heat Wave, Arcanine easily survives at 52% HP (max 32% damage) and guarantees the finish next turn with another Extreme Speed or Gengar in reserve, completely bypassing Rock Slide's 90% accuracy risk.

Heat Wave is the only attack that removes Dragonite before its guaranteed faster-than-Dragonite Rock Slide KO; it also damages Arcanine. Dragonite may Protect, but Scorching Sands lets Dragonite freely Rock Slide and loses immediately. Protect concedes Dragonite’s next Rock Slide threat.

reflections.summary: Bringing Intimidate Arcanine alongside Dragonite allowed safe pivoting against Scarf Garchomp, enabling Ice Spinner to remove Garchomp and double Extreme Speed priority to close out Charizard-Y through sun boost and Tailwind.
reflections.adjustment: Rely directly on targeted double Extreme Speed priority to close out low-HP flying targets instead of clicking spread moves like Rock Slide that can miss.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster facts: Scarf Garchomp, Charizard-Y, Life Orb Primarina, Charti Berry Talonflame. Strategic lesson: Intimidate pivoting combined with Dragonite + Arcanine Extreme Speed priority bypasses opponent Tailwind speed control cleanly.

reflections.summary: Lost because the Charizard-Y/Talonflame endgame was badly exposed to Dragonite and Arcanine: Talonflame fell to Rock Slide, then the weakened Charizard was finished by their combined Extreme Speed. The four brought left too much of the endgame dependent on Charizard-Y despite opposing Rock Slide and dual-priority pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Against the Gengar/Aerodactyl/Dragonite/Arcanine mode, do not plan to close with Charizard-Y. Preserve Primarina as the Dragonite/Arcanine endgame answer and use Charizard earlier rather than treating it as the intended Mega win condition.
reflections.notebook: Opponent selected Mega Gengar, Aerodactyl, Dragonite, and Arcanine in game 2. Dragonite and Arcanine form a dangerous dual-Extreme-Speed cleanup core; do not leave a weakened Charizard-Y as the sole remaining answer. Their Rock Slide users also punish Talonflame/Charizard-Y endgames. Future plan: preserve Primarina for Dragonite/Arcanine and avoid centering the endgame on Charizard-Y against this mode.
